pageTitle: Lesson 20 · Chores and a Tidy Home
eyebrow: Lesson 20 · B1 · Good Manners with Family · 20 câu
heading: Chores and a Tidy Home
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Manners with Family – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 16–21.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Manners with Family (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: Everyone in a family has {chores|chores} to do around the house. Perhaps your dad cooks dinner on Mondays and your mum does the food shopping. Children have jobs too, and it is important to do yours without waiting to be asked.

paras.label: B
paras.text: You may not {feel like|feel like} doing your chores on a Saturday morning. Do them {anyway|anyway}! It shows that you respect your parents' rules and that you care about keeping your home nice for everyone.

paras.label: C
paras.text: Everything has its own place in a home. Fruit goes in the fruit bowl, dirty clothes go in the {laundry|laundry} basket and toys go in the toy box. Use things when you need them, but always put them back where they {belong|belong}. That way, Mum won't {trip over|trip over} your cricket bat, and your little sister can find the comb when she needs it.

paras.label: D
paras.text: If you see a {mess|mess}, clean it up straight away. {Wipe up|wipe up} spilt juice, or pick up the paper that missed the bin. Don't leave it for someone else to do.

paras.label: E
paras.text: Above all, be kind to your family. Help out where you can, respect each other's things and enjoy your dinners together. With good manners, your parents will see that you are {thankful|thankful} for everything they do, and your home will be an even happier place.

parts.title: Part 1 · Which paragraph?
parts.instr: Đoạn nào (A–E) chứa thông tin dưới đây?

items.label: A paragraph that admits chores are not always fun
items.why: Đoạn B: *You may not feel like doing your chores.*

items.label: A paragraph that gives examples of jobs done by parents
items.why: Đoạn A: bố nấu ăn, mẹ đi chợ.

items.label: A paragraph about dealing with a spill
A paragraph that explains how putting things away can prevent accidents
items.why: Đoạn C: mẹ không vấp phải gậy cricket.

items.label: A paragraph that sums up the advice and encourages kindness
items.why: Đoạn E: *Above all, be kind to your family.*

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: According to (A), when should you do your chores?
options: only when your parents remind you
after your friends have gone home
questions.why: *do yours without waiting to be asked.*

questions.q: The writer says you can skip your chores if you don't feel like doing them.
According to (B), what does doing your chores show?
options: respect for your parents' rules and care for your home
that you want more pocket money
that you are better than your brothers and sisters
questions.why: *you respect your parents' rules and… care about keeping your home nice.*

questions.q: Why should you put things back where they belong?
options: so that nobody trips over them and others can find them
so that you can buy new ones
because it is a school rule
so that nobody else can use them
questions.why: *Mum won't trip over… your little sister can find the comb.*

questions.q: According to (D), you should leave paper on the floor if you didn't drop it.
questions.why: Sai. *Don't leave it for someone else to do.*

questions.q: What is the writer's main purpose in (E)?
options: to bring the main ideas together and encourage kindness
to introduce a new rule about chores
to explain how to do the laundry
questions.why: Đoạn E tóm tắt và khích lệ: *Above all, be kind…*

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.alt: A boy sweeps the floor with a broom while a girl wipes a small table with a spray bottle
A girl kneels on the floor wiping up purple juice from a cup that has fallen over

questions.q: Which sentence from (E) best matches this picture?
options: Your home will be an even happier place.
Fruit goes in the fruit bowl.
Don't leave it for someone else to do.
You may not feel like doing your chores.
questions.why: Cái ôm hạnh phúc → *an even happier place.*
questions.alt: A woman and a girl give each other a big, happy hug

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: It was Saturday morning, and my job was to tidy the living room. [1] Then I remembered how tired Mum looked after work every day. [2] When she came downstairs, she couldn't believe her eyes. [3]
options: Mum had already done all the housework for me.
I really wanted to watch cartoons instead.
So I switched off the TV, picked up the toys and wiped the table.
My friend phoned to say the cinema was closed.
"What a lovely surprise!" she said, giving me a big hug.

items.why: Không muốn làm việc nhà (*feel like*).
Nghĩ đến mẹ → làm việc nhà.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *You may not feel like doing your chores* (B). If you **feel like** doing something, you…
questions.why: **Feel like doing sth** = muốn làm gì.

questions.q: *Mum won't trip over your cricket bat* (C). To **trip over** something means to…
options: catch your foot on it and almost fall

questions.q: *…put them back where they belong* (C). **Where they belong** means…
